Keep your elbow straight and raise your arm up to shoulder height. Do not bend your elbow as you are moving, like this (demonstrate).") Development and Preliminary Validity Study of the Upper Extremity Fugl-Meyer Assessment for Telerehabilitation Adapted from Fugl-Meyer A, Jaasko L, Leyman I, Olsson S, Steglind S. The post-stroke hemiplegic patient: a method for evaluation of physical performance. Scandinavian Journal of Rehabilitation Medicine. 1975;7:13-31. 4 Shoulder abduction 0-90*, elbow at 0*, forearm 0 - Immediate supination or elbow flexion pronated 1 - Supination or elbow flexion during movement 2 - Abduction 90*, maintains extension and pronation (Instruction: "Rest your arm at your side, fully straighten your elbow, bring your arm out toward the side to shoulder height, keeping your palm facing the floor, like this (demonstrate).") Shoulder flexion 90-180*, elbow at 0*, 0 - Immediate abduction or elbow flexion pronation-supination at 0* 1 - Abduction or elbow flexion during movement 2 - Flexion 180*, no shoulder abduction or elbow flexion (Instruction: "Hold your arm straight out in front of your body, straighten your elbow, point your thumb up toward the ceiling. Bring your arm up as far as you can, like this (demonstrate).") Pronation/supination, elbow at 0*, shoulder at 30-90* 0 - No pronation/supination, starting position flexion impossible 1 - Limited pronation/supination, maintains start position 2 - Full pronation/supination, maintains starting position (Instruction: "Straighten your arm in front of your body, keep your elbow straight and turn your palm up and down as far as you can go, like this (demonstrate)".) Subtotal IV (max 6) Biceps, triceps, finger flexors 0 - 2 of 3 reflexes markedly hyperactive or 0 points in part IV 1 - 1 reflex markedly hyperactive or at least 2 reflexes lively 2 - Maximum of 1 reflex lively, none hyperactive

Development and Preliminary Validity Study of the Upper Extremity Fugl-Meyer Assessment for Telerehabilitation Adapted from Fugl-Meyer A, Jaasko L, Leyman I, Olsson S, Steglind S. The post-stroke hemiplegic patient: a method for evaluation of physical performance. Scandinavian Journal of Rehabilitation Medicine. 1975;7:13-31. 5 Subtotal V (max 2) TOTAL A (Subtotals I-V, max 36) Wrist stability (elbow 90˚) 0 - Less than 15* active dorsiflexion Apply resistance at 15˚ dorsiflexion. The elbow may 1 - Dorsiflexion 15*, no resistance tolerated be supported if needed. Lift your hand and hold it 2 - Maintains dorsiflexion against resistance there, keep your elbow bent. Instruction: "Place your arm at your side in the shape of an "L", palm facing down; without moving the rest of your arm, extend and hold your wrist upwards, like this (demonstrate).") Wrist flexion/extension (elbow 90˚) 0 - Cannot perform volitionally The elbow may be supported if needed. 1 - limited active range of motion Lift your hand up and down, keep your elbow bent. 2 - full active range of motion, smoothly (Instruction: "Place your arm at your side in the shape of an "L", palm facing down; without moving the rest of your arm, extend your wrist all the way up and down, like this (demonstrate).") Wrist stability (elbow 0˚) 0 - Less than 15* active dorsiflexion Apply resistance at 15˚ dorsiflexion. The elbow may 1 - Dorsiflexion 15*, no resistance tolerated be supported if needed. 2 - Maintain dorsiflexion against resistance (Instruction: Lift your hand, hold the position with your arm straight.) Wrist flexion/extension (elbow 0˚) 0 - Cannot perform volitionally The elbow may be supported if needed. Lift your hand 1 - Limited active range of motion up and down with your arm straight. 2 - full range of motion, smoothly (Instruction: "Straighten your arm in front of your body; keep your elbow straight, extend and hold your wrist upwards, like this (demonstrate)")

Development and Preliminary Validity Study of the Upper Extremity Fugl-Meyer Assessment for Telerehabilitation Adapted from Fugl-Meyer A, Jaasko L, Leyman I, Olsson S, Steglind S. The post-stroke hemiplegic patient: a method for evaluation of physical performance. Scandinavian Journal of Rehabilitation Medicine. 1975;7:13-31. 7 b. Thumb adduction 0 - Cannot be performed 1st CMC, MCP, IP at 0*, scrap of paper between thumb 1 - Can hold paper but not against tug and 2nd MCP joint 2 - Can hold paper against a tug (Instruction: Place your arm at your side in the shape of an "L". "Hold this paper between your thumb and index finger keeping them both straight; don't let me pull it away, like this (demonstrate).") c. Pincer grasp, opposition 0 - Cannot be performed pulpa of the thumb against the pulpa of 2nd finger, 1 - Can hold pencil but not against tug pencil, tug away 2 - Can hold pencil against a tug (Instruction: Place your arm at your side in the shape of an "L". "Take the pencil from me with the pads of your thumb and index finger; don't let me pull it away, like this (demonstrate).") d. Cylinder grasp 0 - cannot be performed cylinder shaped object (small can) tug away, 1 - can hold cylinder but not against tug opposition of thumb and fingers 2 - can hold cylinder against a tug (Instruction: Place your arm at your side in the shape of an "L". Take the can from me with your thumb and index fingers wrapped around it; don't let me pull it away, like this (demonstrate).") e. Spherical grasp 0 - cannot be performed fingers in abduction/flexion, thumb opposed, tennis 1 - can hold ball but not against tug ball, tug away 2 - can hold ball against a tug (Instruction: Place your arm at your side in the shape of an "L." Take this tennis ball from my hand with your fingers; don't let me pull it out of your hand, like this (demonstrate).") TOTAL VII (max 14) TOTAL C (max 14)
